title: A zoom on a cropped video shows exactly the box you drew
goal: On a video that has been cropped, drawing a zoom box around something and playing it should fill the visible picture with exactly what was inside the box. Today it zooms far further in than the box and shows a different part of the picture, so the zoom cannot be aimed on a cropped recording.
notes:
User's words: "I make a zoom track on a video.. The video was cropped. I position the zoom on some text. When I play it, rather than zooming in on the rect around text, it zooms way too far in, not matching at all what the rect was". Screenshots 2026-10-06 20.16.40 (box over 'The Role of AI vs. Humans in Code', label 517%, box about half the visible picture's width) and 20.17.42 (played: only 'Role of AI vs. Hu' / 'Code Generation' / 'AI tools like GitHub', far tighter than the box, in a smaller square).

SUSPECT from code reading, not reproduced: the box is kept as a fraction of the clip layer's whole frame (EditorState+Zoom.swift:390-396, and pointer mapping :493-494), and the renderer cuts that fraction out of the picture and scales it to fill the layer frame (DocumentRenderer.swift:1127-1143, after the layer-local crop at :1114-1125). If 'cropped' here is a canvas/document crop, the layer frame is still the whole recording and the canvas shows only part of it: the box percent (517%) is measured against the whole recording, and the zoom fills the whole frame of which only the middle is visible, so it reads as zooming far too far in. If it is the clip's own layer crop, check that layer.frame and the post-crop image agree (fraction of frame vs fraction of cropped image). Model: ClipZoom window(atMS:) and Layer.zoomWindow (PhotonzCore/ClipZoom.swift:313-350). Fix likely: map the box against the VISIBLE picture (frame intersected with the canvas, or the crop) and convert to the window in the picture's own fractions. Related, done: a-zoom-region-that-frames-a-spot-and-can-follow, scrubbing-a-recording-shows-what-the-zoom-does-a.
acceptance: Reproduce first at Next defaults with the user's steps: crop a recording (try each way the app offers to crop a video: the canvas/document crop and the clip's own crop), add a zoom, place its box around a block of text, play. Photograph the box and the played frame for each crop kind, and record the box's percent label against the measured magnification

For every crop kind, the played (and scrubbed and exported) frame at the zoom's full point shows exactly the box's contents filling the visible picture: the box's four corners land on the picture's four edges within 2 px, MEASURED and written in the audit
The percent on the box equals the real magnification of the visible picture (visible width / box width), MEASURED
If the box's aspect differs from the visible picture's, the zoom behaves the same documented way it does on an uncropped video (fit or fill), and the box shows that shape while dragging
Follow Cursor and Suggest Zooms aim at the same visible picture on a cropped video
Existing zooms on uncropped videos are unchanged; zooms already saved on cropped videos are migrated or read so they show what their box showed, and the audit says which
Unit tests in PhotonzCore for the box to window mapping with each crop kind; a walk at Next defaults crops, zooms on a marked spot and checks the played frame
Audit under queue/audits/; anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar (queue/bin/follow-up-bar.md), and written into this task's log if it does not.

log.note: Adversarial review before building: a Premiere/Screen Studio user expects the zoom box to frame what is ON SCREEN, so the box must live on the visible picture and keep its shape; the app had three ways to crop a video (canvas crop, clip crop, keyed crop edges) and the box was measured against the clip's whole laid-out frame in all of them. Nothing the mock-free surface assumes is missing, so no prerequisite filed.

Reproduced on old code with three new walks (probe, Next defaults, no flags): canvas crop: corners missed by 458 px, box said 533% and really 333%, 17.7% of pixels wrong; keyed crop: 416 px, 533% vs 333%, 20.4% wrong; clip's own crop: right on this Mac (frames read full size). Unit test also showed a clip-cropped frame read small, and any cropped picture drawn at 2x, drew the wrong part or nothing.

Fixed: ZoomStage (PhotonzCore/ZoomStage.swift) + stage-aware ClipZoom; spot = point of the recording, scale = how far into what is seen. Renderer crop read against the bitmap in hand. Click ripples through the clip's crop. Old documents converted on open (aimedAtWhatIsSeen). After: all three walks corners within 0.0 px, 370% label = 370% real both ways, 2-3.4% pixels differ (resampling); canvas == export at every scrubbed frame. Existing 8 zoom/click walks green; Scripts/test.sh 11665 tests green.

left rough (not filed, below the bar): after a canvas crop the clip's selection outline and handles still hang off the canvas edge (pre-existing, visible in 2026-10-07-zoom-on-a-cropped-video-2.png); zoomStageInHand redraws the document per query, fine for a recording, worth caching if a big composite shows lag while framing.

A zoom on a cropped recording (canvas crop, clip crop, keyed crop edges) now fills the visible picture with exactly the box: ZoomStage in PhotonzCore, spot on the recording and scale against what is seen, old files converted on open; renderer reads a picture's crop against the bitmap in hand (fixes small reads and 2x). Reproduced first on old code (458 px off, 533% said vs 333% real); after, three new walks at Next defaults measure corners within 0.0 px, label = real magnification, canvas == export. 16 core + 4 render unit tests; Scripts/test.sh 11665 green; 8 existing zoom/click walks green. Audit queue/audits/2026-10-07-zoom-on-a-cropped-video.json. Commit ac035991.
